advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Soften the docs' cross-process atomicity claim, or use an O_APPEND os.write of the encoded line to make the single-append guarantee real.
evidence: docs/llm-framework.md:513: 'Each row is written with a single append of one complete line, so concurrent gate runs interleave rows without corrupting one'

src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:464: `with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:` then `handle.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")` — buffered text-mode append, not an atomic O_APPEND write() of a bounded record
ABSENCE: no os.O_APPEND / os.write / file lock is used to make the append atomic across concurrent gate processes
advisory.finding: The docs assert 'Each row is written with a single append of one complete line, so concurrent gate runs interleave rows without corrupting one', but record() uses Python's buffered open(path,'a') without O_APPEND-atomic guarantees; a single logical line can be split across multiple write() syscalls and, for lines exceeding PIPE_BUF, concurrent multi-process appends can interleave/corrupt. The safety claim is stronger than the implementation guarantees.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm repo_root() is the intended anchor for the default sink even when the gate reviews a different checkout, and document that the sink lives under rebar's repo root, not the target's.
evidence: ABSENCE: _resolve_sink/record() never consult the RunRequest target or cfg.repo_path when choosing the default sink location
advisory.finding: The default gate sink is anchored to rebar.config.repo_root() (via _repo_root_for_default_sink), not to the reviewed target's cfg.repo_path/req.target. When a gate runs against a checkout other than rebar's own repo root, usage rows land in rebar's repo .rebar/usage.jsonl rather than the target checkout's, which may surprise an operator retrieving spend from the checkout they reviewed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update `record()`'s opening docstring line to reflect that the sink is resolved by `_resolve_sink` (env var OR default gate sink), not just `$REBAR_USAGE_LOG`.
evidence: record() docstring opening (context): "Append one usage record for a single LLM call to ``$REBAR_USAGE_LOG`` (JSONL)."
Module docstring added: "With that var unset, a run inside a GATE SESSION falls back to ``<repo root>/.rebar/usage.jsonl`` when that directory already exists"
record() no-op line changed to: "No-op when :func:`_resolve_sink` finds no sink (the default outside a gate session)"
advisory.finding: The `record()` docstring's opening line still says it appends "to ``$REBAR_USAGE_LOG`` (JSONL)", but the same change adds a default gate-session sink (`<repo root>/.rebar/usage.jsonl`) that `record()` now writes to when the env var is unset — so the opening line names a destination that is no longer the only one.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the first line to reference the resolved sink, e.g. "Append one usage record for a single LLM call to the resolved JSONL sink (see :func:`_resolve_sink`)."

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a success-path assertion that the recorded token counters (input/output/cache/requests) match the provider's _extract_usage figures and are not overwritten by the reducer's shape, so widening _SHAPE_FIELDS to include token totals fails the test.
evidence: shape_only docstring: 'Deliberately drops the reducer's TOKEN totals ... Merging the approximation over them would silently corrupt cost accounting, so the filter, not the caller's care, is what prevents it.' (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:245-248)
runner.py success path: 'usage.update(usage_log.shape_only(shape))' with the comment 'Overwriting those with the approximation would silently corrupt cost accounting.'

test_the_success_row_records_the_tool_call_shape_too asserts only row['tool_calls']==3 and row['tool_calls_distinct']==3 (tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py:132-134) — no assertion on any token counter's provenance

_extract_usage produces the provider 'requests'/token counts (src/rebar/llm/structured_run.py:475-484) while run_shape recomputes its own token totals (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:194-201), so the two sources are genuinely distinct and the drop is a real, assertable behavior
advisory.finding: The success-path contract that shape_only() must NOT overwrite the provider's billable token counters is untested. test_the_success_row_records_the_tool_call_shape_too asserts tool_calls/tool_calls_distinct are present but never asserts the row's input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_*/requests are the provider's _extract_usage figures rather than the reducer's message-derived approximation. A mutation that added token fields to _SHAPE_FIELDS (or used usage.update(shape) directly) — the exact 'silently corrupt cost accounting' regression the diff exists to prevent — would pass every test in the new file.
scenarios: A future edit adds token fields to _SHAPE_FIELDS or replaces the shape_only() filter with a raw merge; billable figures on success rows are silently replaced by message-derived approximations and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_the_success_row_records_the_tool_call_shape_too (or a dedicated test), assert the row's token/requests values equal the provider usage the success path started from, or add a unit test on shape_only() asserting no _TOKEN_FIELDS/'requests' key survives its filter.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that calls usage_log.record() with a usage dict carrying only token counters (no shape keys) and asserts the written row OMITS every _SHAPE_FIELDS key.
evidence: record() comment: 'Defaulting them to 0 would make a caller that never reduced any messages ... claim `tool_calls: 0` ... An absent key says the only true thing: not measured.' (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:449-453)
the write loop 'for field in _SHAPE_FIELDS: if field in usage: row[field] = usage[field]' (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:456-458) is only ever exercised with shape PRESENT in the new tests
existing analogous omission test: 'assert "model" not in row' (tests/unit/test_usage_log.py:126-127) — no equivalent 'assert "tool_calls" not in row' exists
advisory.finding: The 'absent means not measured' contract for the shape fields — explicitly documented as 'load-bearing rather than tidy' — is not tested. No test drives record() (or a run) with a usage dict lacking shape keys and asserts the row OMITS tool_calls et al. rather than writing 0. The analogous omission for model/provider IS pinned (test_record_defaults_omit_model_provider), leaving this load-bearing branch uncovered.
scenarios: A refactor changes the shape write to default absent fields to 0; a shapeless caller's row would then falsely assert 'this run used no tools' and be summed into aggregates as fact, with no failing test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a record()-level unit test: record({'input_tokens':1,'requests':1}, op='x', outcome=OK) and assert none of tool_calls/tool_calls_distinct/max_consecutive_repeat/top_repeated_tool_calls/finish_reason appear in the row.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that a run whose ModelResponse carries a finish_reason records that finish_reason on the row (e.g. a budget-exhaustion or length case).
evidence: 'finish_reason' listed in _SHAPE_FIELDS (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:43) and written when present (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:456-458)
no occurrence of finish_reason anywhere in tests/unit/test_usage_log_run_shape_aec1.py (fixtures build ModelResponse/TextPart with no finish_reason set: lines 81-102)
the diff's docstring names finish_reason among 'These exist because the token counters cannot tell a LOOP from genuine BREADTH' (docs/llm-framework.md run-shape section)
advisory.finding: finish_reason is added to _SHAPE_FIELDS and written by record(), but no test asserts it reaches the row on either path. The FunctionModel responses in the fixtures set no finish_reason, so this newly persisted shape field is never exercised end-to-end by the file whose stated purpose is to pin the recorded run shape.
scenarios: A regression that dropped finish_reason from the write allowlist (as the pre-aec1 code dropped the whole shape) would not be caught by this suite.
advisory.suggested_fix: Give _looping_model or a new fixture a ModelResponse(finish_reason='length') (or 'tool_call') and assert row['finish_reason'] equals it on the recorded row.
